# Bounded observer-fidelity control

This is a synthetic, zero-capability observer diagnostic, not product qualification. It does not change the original 176 cases, their acceptance rules, the frozen independent cohort, or the already consumed one-shot CAP_SYS_PTRACE grant.

The first push from PR69 HEAD `0f018fbee472e14e30584c9d03cfa0817e7c8081` can run this ordinary Actions check once. Both observers and the synthetic process start with zero effective, permitted, inheritable and ambient capabilities and inherit `no_new_privs`. The inherited bounding set is reported, not falsely claimed empty. No sudo, setcap, host setting, repository credential or user data is used. The source archives come from the official strace site and are pinned by exact size and SHA-256. Nothing is installed system-wide.

The comparison is strace 6.8 versus 6.12, which first includes upstream fix [c7e0ea6](https://github.com/strace/strace/commit/c7e0ea6d712eb214dafe7e9eae57661d9a427ea7). Instrumentation records existing wait results, GET_SYSCALL_INFO return length/op and the register fallback already performed by the observer. It adds no ptrace operations and restores errno around diagnostic output. The old private `sched_attr` tag is renamed to build with newer glibc; its layout and decoded values are unchanged. All instrumentation/compatibility diffs and source hashes are retained. Observer output timing is affected by logging; these are explicitly instrumented test builds, not the original CI binaries.

The C probe performs 100 bounded teardown cycles with three sleeping sibling threads while its parent makes recognizable metadata calls on one owned, one-byte fixture. Each observer run has a 30-second wall bound, 25 CPU-second limit, 256 MiB address-space limit, 32 MiB per-file limit and disabled core dumps. Timeout or requested interruption stops only its freshly created process group; exception-safe kill/wait/reap records partial results. The tracer has a checked parent-death SIGKILL and parent-PID race check; EXITKILL then kills its tracees if the controller disappears. An empty-child check confirms scoped cleanup. Raw syscall output, terminal records, observer records, workload status and cleanup status remain evidence, including failures.

The analysis needs positive kernel NONE/stale-union and corrected-fallback observations. Successful workload completion or non-recurrence alone is inconclusive. Even a positive control does not recover an old opaque/unfinished syscall, authorize a new product path, prove the FD handoff, or qualify the whole Python/Go/Rust operation. Fresh complete product evidence remains required under separately approved privileges, if any.

In the current cloud execution environment, both local controls were unrun: PTRACE_TRACEME returned EPERM during strace's EXITKILL capability probe, before workload launch. No trace was produced; cleanup was empty. This is a host tracing limit, not a product failure. The Actions check is the authorized ordinary-environment verification route; it grants no tracing capability.
